Proposition selected for the requested campaign

raw_plan.interpretation: Treat this as a one-email acquisition campaign for a new buyer in the selected Customer Success / Ops segment. Because no individual company has been qualified, address teams conditionally when they are rebuilding customer intake rather than assuming the recipient already has the documented problem or a particular software stack.

intent.desired_action: Create a free Tally form and test a request-type-specific intake flow.

raw_plan.reader: A Customer Success or Operations buyer at a fast-growing SaaS company who may be rebuilding how customer requests are collected and routed.
raw_plan.reader_segment: Customer Success / Ops teams revamping intake forms at fast-growing SaaS companies
raw_plan.reader_scope: The qualified slice is teams whose intake questions need to change by request type. Zapier is relevant only when its published catalogue includes the team's downstream destination; exact connector depth and field mapping remain unverified.
raw_plan.promise: Tally can give a CS or Ops team one structured intake form that changes its questions by request type and can pass submissions into downstream tools through Zapier when a suitable connection exists.
raw_plan.orientation: Tally is a no-code form builder a Customer Success or Ops person can use to build a structured customer request or feedback form and pass submissions into the tools their team already works in.
raw_plan.arc: In one email, move from the familiar limitation of universal intake to Tally's concrete conditional-logic mechanism, show the documented downstream route, answer the fit concern honestly, and invite the reader to build one free form.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: A solution-aware buyer does not need a lesson on why forms exist. The email should lead with the most relevant documented operation: changing the questions according to request type. Zapier then makes the proposition useful within an existing process, while the free offer lowers the cost of testing it. The email must not imply that Tally has already reduced resolution time or staff-submitted tickets, because those outcomes are not established. One applicable objection is addressed: submissions can connect through Zapier's catalogue, but the exact destination connector and field-level mapping still need checking. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign is the unreadable source in a readable form or verification of its missing details.

emails.selection_reason: Conditional logic directly addresses the documented intake-design problem: different request types need different information. It gives this reader a concrete operational reason to try Tally, while Zapier provides a documented route into an existing workflow.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team is rebuilding intake, it can use one form to present request-type-specific questions instead of giving every requester the same field set, then use a suitable Zapier connection to pass submissions downstream.
value_case.mechanism: The team configures conditional logic so the form adapts to the requester's inputs. Tally's Zapier integration can connect submissions to apps in Zapier's published catalogue.
decision_conditions: Unlimited forms and submissions are free only within Tally's fair usage guidelines.
The downstream benefit depends on the required destination being available through the documented Zapier catalogue.
The evidence does not establish the depth of any individual connector or field-level mapping into a particular ticketing system.

claim_conditions: Frame the intake situation conditionally rather than asserting that this recipient currently uses a universal form.
Treat the exact question set as a design choice for the team, not an automatic Tally outcome.
Qualify the free offer with Tally's fair usage guidelines.

emails.job: Get the reader to create one free form and test whether conditional branching can represent a real customer-request flow.
emails.single_idea: Tally lets a CS or Ops team build one intake form that asks different questions for different request types, with a documented Zapier route for sending submissions into downstream tools when a suitable connection exists.
emails.felt_need: A universal request form does not always collect the specific information the person handling each type of request needs.
emails.status_quo: Observed teams create distinct intake forms for different request types, with the person actioning each request defining the information to collect.
emails.mechanism: Use conditional logic to make the form adapt to the request type and inputs. If the required destination is supported in Zapier's catalogue, use the published Zapier integration as the downstream route.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is the stronger alternative if the team prefers separate owner-designed forms rather than one branching form: Tally supports creating and revising forms with plain-language instructions, while the free offer permits unlimited forms and submissions within fair usage guidelines.

value_case.reader_benefit: A CS or Ops team can create separate request-type forms and revise them in plain language, without a documented per-form or per-submission allowance under the free offer while usage remains within the fair usage guidelines.
value_case.mechanism: Tally AI can generate, edit and fix forms from plain-language instructions, and the free offer includes unlimited forms and submissions within fair usage guidelines.
decision_conditions: Unlimited forms and submissions remain free only within Tally's fair usage guidelines.

claim_conditions: Do not infer that plain-language editing eliminates form-design work.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: When separate request-type forms suit the operating model better, Tally lets the team generate and revise those forms in plain language and keep unlimited forms and submissions free within fair usage guidelines.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: The person actioning each request needs an intake form designed around the information required for that request type.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Observed teams maintain different forms for different request types.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Give Tally AI plain-language instructions to generate, edit or fix each form; create as many forms and collect as many submissions as needed within the free offer's fair usage guidelines.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: supporting request-specific intake necessarily makes the form-tool allowance a constraint. After: Tally documents unlimited free forms and submissions within fair usage guidelines, plus plain-language form generation and editing.
must_not_say: Do not claim Tally AI automatically knows which fields each actioning owner needs.

alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether Tally's plain-language form creation and editing are suitable for producing one request-type-specific intake form.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The action lets the reader begin creating a form under an offer that documents unlimited forms and submissions within fair usage guidelines.

events.preview_text: Build one intake form that adapts by request type, then test a route into your workflow.
events.body:
If your team is rebuilding customer intake, start with one real request flow. Choose the request types, then decide which questions the person actioning each one needs answered.

Tally is an online form builder with conditional logic. You can configure one form to adapt its questions to the request type and the requester’s previous inputs.

That means billing, onboarding and technical requests can follow different paths inside the same form, with the question set designed by your team.

When a suitable destination is available in Zapier’s catalogue, Tally’s published Zapier integration can pass submissions into that downstream app.

Build the first flow and see whether the branching fits your intake process. Tally offers unlimited forms and submissions for free within its fair usage guidelines.
